ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: the council's priorities
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What the advisor watches, from the food against the winter to a promise about to break, and what its buttons do
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Start at the top of the list. Gentle advice sits low and never shows among the alerts.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Priorities, in the Colony section of the council window, lists what the colony needs right now, worst first. The advisor looks again every hour, and each piece of advice says why it matters, what helps, and a rotating tip. It never acts on its own: every button only shows, plans or opens something for you to decide on.

table.li: Show me | Goes to the people, rooms or things the advice is about.
Plan the room | Opens the room planner on the fitting room, at the size the colony needs.
Upgrade the room | Opens the planner on a room you've built: pick it, and only what's missing is planned.
Go to | Opens the council page that deals with it: Decrees for a decree or an empty office, World for a mission or a world event, Wishes for a promise, Calendar for a day.

Its own action | Some advice can do the first step for you: show the mission's quest, open the camp's letter, open the Work tab, plan wall lamps where beds lie dark, or plan chairs and lamps at a workshop's benches.
Read more | Opens the Almanac page on it.

li.heading: What it watches

table.li: Food | the food against the coming winter, spoiling food, blight, ripe crops before frost, a week without fruit or vegetables, food that won't keep through a mild winter in a tribe or a manor
Shelter and warmth | beds and barracks, cold or hot months ahead, the weather's troubles, stores left under the open sky before winter, firewood short of what the fires will burn by spring
Health | doctors, medicine and a hospital, the only doctor with nobody to tend them, convalescents back at work, a plague or a famine in the region while the colony is short of what helps
Comfort | rooms without light, beds no light reaches, meals eaten without a table, recreation and its hours, strain near breaking, loneliness, clothes worn to rags

The council | wishes about to lapse, promises about to break, trust, a decree whose reason has passed while its moods still cost, an office empty when it matters (no physician with the sick in bed, no reeve at harvest, no keeper of days before a day)

Rimfolk's world | a mission near its deadline with its goods not all there, a camp growing tense or hungry, a camp's question left waiting, a calendar day coming round, and one tomorrow with nothing laid by for it

Rooms, gently | a dining room with too few seats or too cramped, barracks that could become bedrooms, a hospital without what you've researched, a rec room with too little to do, a noble's bedroom short of the title, a kitchen with one stove for too many, a full freezer, a workshop with dark benches or no chairs, a prison cell without comfort

li.after: Defenses, power, fire risk, insects under the mountain, the dead, prisoners' needs and an idle research bench are watched too. Where a newer piece of advice says more, the older one steps aside: dark bedrooms and workshops have their own advice with lamps to plan, a mild winter's food has its own, and a calendar day tomorrow with nothing laid by replaces the plain reminder.

li.heading: When it speaks
li.text: A mission is pressing in its last two days, or its last quarter when that is under four. A decree is called costly only once what it was enacted for has passed (the food is no longer low, the threat is days gone) while more people are against it than for it and the moods add up to a loss of three or more. The winter advice comes within about twenty days of the cold, for a tribal or medieval colony, and only when the winter won't freeze the stores on its own. A kitchen has outgrown its stove at eight people with one stove, two cooks and fewer meals than mouths; a freezer is full when 17 of every 20 storage spots are taken while 30 or more pieces of food spoil outside it; a dining room is cramped when its space is rather tight or under two and a half for each of five or more.

li.heading: The plan: the colony's next steps
li.text: The Plan page (Planning, then Plan) keeps a short, ordered list of what to do next. Each hour the council proposes steps from what it watches: the priorities above, the defense advice and an idle research bench, at most eight at once, most pressing first. Take a step into the plan, or let it go (it isn't proposed again for a fortnight); add steps of your own, with a room plan if it's a room to build; move them up and down, or order the whole plan by urgency. Each step opens what does it: the room planner (at a suggested spot), the defense plan to place, the research to start, or the thing on the map. A step is done when you say so, or when the need behind it has passed for three hours running; done steps stay listed for five days. The first step shows on This week and in the council panel; a step under the mouse shows on the map what it points at. "Ground plan" draws the plan's rooms and the proposals on the map together, each at the spot that fits best with the ones before it kept clear, with a button that opens the planner there (a click on the drawn outline does the same). Switch the page off under "The colony's next steps".

li.heading: The base, looked over
li.text: The Base page (Planning, then Base) is the council's walk round the base, once an hour or when you ask. Rooms: a kitchen far from the freezer or the dining room, a workshop far from its store, a hospital far from the gate, a barn far from the fields; bedrooms or the hospital right by a workshop or a barn, a prison cell by the bedrooms. Walks: bedrooms a long way from the nearest dining room on average. Doors: a door with the same room on both sides or no wall beside it, and a freezer door that opens into a warm room or the open air with no airlock between. Walls: short stubs hanging off a proper wall that separate nothing (never a pillar on its own, a wall with a lamp on it, or one holding up a roof by itself). Conduits and pipes: runs that lead from a fork or a used piece to an end with nothing on it, conduit joined to nothing at all, and the same for Dubs Bad Hygiene's and Vanilla Expanded's pipes. Stores: stockpiles that take everything, goods lying about that no store accepts (with a button that lays out a stockpile for them by the store room), a bench far from the nearest store of its bills' materials (with a button that lays out a little store beside it, set to prefer them; never for raw food or corpses, which belong in the cold), one kind of goods accepted in three rooms or more, and stores whose filter allows nothing. Each finding says where to look; the doors, stubs, conduits and pipes have a button that gives the deconstruct orders, which you cancel on the map like any other, and a room far from what it belongs with has "Plan the room", which opens the planner on the cheaper of the pair (a freezer by the kitchen, a store by the workshop) at a spot found beside the other. The findings are also proposed as steps on the Plan page. A little map of the base on the left shows the rooms by their use, the walls, the doors and the rock, with every finding marked in its part's colour; while the page is open the findings are drawn on the real map as well, the rooms a finding is about outlined and a line to what they're far from, and the finding under the mouse in full. "Show on the map" keeps them drawn with the window closed.

li.heading: What you could make
li.text: The Making page (Planning, then Making) reads the recipes of every bench the colony has and checks them against the stock, so any mod's benches and recipes count by themselves. "You could make now" lists, bench by bench, each batch the stock allows that has no bill set for it and whose product the colony has fewer than sixty of, the staples first (meals, medicine, components, blocks, cloth) and of clothes and weapons only the dearest two; "Set a bill, until N" adds the bill to the bench, make until the colony has that many. "Harvests and finds nothing here uses" lists what the colony has a fair amount of that has a particular use at a bench the colony lacks (hops for a brewery, psychoid leaves for a drug lab, chunks for a stonecutter), the bench and the product, and the research it waits on, with a button to open it or to build the bench. Benches standing without bills are named at the bottom. A batch under the mouse outlines its bench on the map. The chains: "Wanted for the building and the bills" names each material the blueprints and frames are short of beyond the stock, or that a bill on some bench is waiting on with none in stock, and the bench here that makes it, with a bill sized to the want (the stock, the want and a fifth more, never under the usual count); bills waiting on an ingredient the colony has none of are listed with the bill that would feed them, or told what to grow, mine or trade for. A batch something waits on is listed first and marked in gold, whatever the colony's stock of it. Bill counts for meals and medicine grow with the colony: three days of two meals a head, two medicine a head, within bounds. Each chain is followed to the end: down through the recipes of the benches you have, each part a link of its own, four links at most and never round in a circle, each link with what there is and what is wanted, its use and make in a day (meals eaten, medicine spent, what the active bills take and give, what the growing zones yield) and how long its stock lasts, the bench and recipe that would make it best (the best able hand's skill, less a point for every twenty cells from the materials' store, plus a little for the product an hour of work gives), how long a batch takes, and the whole chain's lead time; "Set the chain's bills" sets them all, the parts' first, each to make until the next link has what it takes and three days of its use. A link no bench makes but a plant you can sow yields says how many cells to sow, and "Sow it" adds them beside the zone that grows it or lays out a new zone near the fields.

li.heading: Automations: the council does it for you
li.text: Under Building in the settings, each of these is its own switch, off unless you turn it on; switched on, the council does each hour what it would otherwise only suggest, tells you in a quiet message, keeps a log on the check-myself page, and never acts while there is fighting on the map or over your own orders. "Bills for what the colony lacks": a make-until bill for a staple the colony lacks and can make (meals, medicine, components) and for whatever the blueprints and the other bills wait on, two an hour at most; a bill you remove isn't set again for a fortnight. "Urgent steps go straight into the plan": a step proposed at a high level or above is taken into the plan at once. "An idle research bench takes up the next project": the cheapest project of the colony's own era, never one that pushes it into the next era; pick another whenever you like. "Goods nobody stores get a stockpile": the stores review's stockpile for them, every five days at most. "What serves nothing is taken down": the base review's take-down orders for wall stubs, dead conduit and pipe ends, and doors between the same room. "Dark bedrooms and benches get lamps and chairs planned": the advisor's own planning buttons, once a day. "Trees are marked for chopping when firewood runs short": the nearest mature trees outside your growing zones, five to twelve by how short the wood is, once a day. "A thing a plant yields gets sown for": a chain's link that no bench makes but a plant yields, with no zone growing it, gets its cells sown, once every ten days per thing. The bills automation has its own switches for meals, medicine, components and the chains (link by link, the parts' bills first). A materials budget a day (the worth of the things built) bounds the blueprints the automations place, and daily caps bound the take-down orders and the chopping marks. At the bottom of the Making page, every automation says what it would do now, on or off, and the last things done are listed, each undone at a click: the bill off the bench (and not set again for a fortnight), the step back to proposed, the research pick, the zone, the orders, the blueprints, the marks. Everything the council does is undone the ordinary way as well.
